findings.text: — §4's two-assertion test cannot fail against the base revision:

findings.reason: the deliverable names a behaviour the code already has and omits the branch that caused the incident, so an implementer has nothing to change in `_session_from_followers` and will report the section implemented on unchanged logic.
findings.text: §4 states the mechanism as "resolves the session it reports from the hook payload's own harness session … It never takes a follower child the host holds for another session as its own", which is a description of what `_session_from_followers` (reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py) already does; the live defect is the second branch it falls to: `read_followers` returns every session's registration sorted by name, and on the first row that is not an exact match the function returns `record` whenever `_descends_from(follower.parent_pid, claude_pid)` holds, so another session's follower whose host descends from the caller's Claude process is adopted before the caller's own registration is ever scanned

findings.reason: either the node amends its write scope mid-flight to reach promotion_gate.py, or it lands a return-shape change that writes a tuple into a persisted record field, and the plan as written permits both.
findings.text: §2's mechanism ("`write` … reports the per-run files it changed beside its new version") changes `write`'s return to a pair while the same paragraph says "Every other caller of `write` is unchanged"; `reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:1051` does `new_version = ledger.write(...)` and stores that value at line 1075 as `"ledger_version": new_version`, so a pair lands in the gate report's ledger version field, and `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1469` and `reckon/crew/routing.py:3124` are outside the section's declared write paths (`reckon/ledger.py` and the new test)

findings.reason: one gate spanning both closes neither, so a node that gets the ask-ownership right and the settle policy wrong is closed on a verdict that proves neither change.
findings.text: §3 holds two deliverables with different failure modes and different files: the ask-ownership and census-reading changes in `reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py`, and a change to the host's restart policy in `reckon/crew/session_host.py` ("settles that child" for a pair another live host already serves). The second is the duplicate-follower defect, not the misrouted-ask defect the section title names

findings.reason: the followup is the plan's next-action record, and as written it under-dispatches two thirds of the remaining work.
findings.text: the plan's only open followup names §2 alone in both `data-recommends-skill` and its command block, while its body says "§2, §3 and §4 … can run together"; a coordinator following the invocation dispatches one of the three implementable sections and §3 and §4 reach the outcome zero times

findings.reason: the file resolves and the call site is a legitimate pointer, so a reader reaches the right module; correcting the line costs nothing but changes no work.
findings.text: §4 cites `_session_from_followers` "(near line 865)", which is the call inside `locate_session`; the definition is at `reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:439`, 426 lines away, and the `session_id` parenthetical at 867 is accurate

response_events.note: §4's first case now uses two followers that both descend from the caller's Claude process, the other session's sorted first, which the base revision resolves wrongly.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the `_session_from_followers` anchor in §4 names line 865, which is the call site in `locate_session`, not the function definition at line 439.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §4's done-when passes on the unmodified code, because the hook already resolves the harness session through `_session_from_followers` before any follower-child fallback.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate log under the three sections is written under the run directory and must start with its revision and literal command and end in `EXIT=`, which is a durable path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the three new test filenames and section titles name the mechanism, and no ticket, plan label or version tag reaches a symbol or path.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2 says every other caller of `write` is unchanged, but reporting the changed files beside the version changes `write`'s return shape and `reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:1051` stores that return as `ledger_version`.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §3 carries the host's restart policy (a change in `reckon/crew/session_host.py`) as a second deliverable beside the ask-ownership fix in `dispatch_watch.py`.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — followup f-acpwowio-001 declares only §2 in both `data-recommends-skill` and its prompt block while its body says §2, §3 and §4 run together.
